rawFindings.title: Incorrect global replacement of '%' in script command string
rawFindings.explanation: The original code replaces all occurrences of '%' in the script command string with the joined ordered package names using a global regular expression (/g). The new code replaces only the first occurrence by passing a string '%' to mout.string.replace, which calls String.replace and replaces only the first '%'. This changes behavior unintentionally if the script contains multiple '%' placeholders, leading to incomplete substitution and potentially malformed commands.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep the global replacement by using a global regular expression like /%/g instead of a string to replace all '%' occurrences. E.g., change to mout.string.replace(config.scripts[action], /%/g, orderedPackages.join(' ')).

rawFindings.title: Test updates do not cover multiple '%' replacement case
rawFindings.explanation: The tests were modified to use script names with only a single '%' placeholder (e.g., 'preinstall_%' instead of 'preinstall_%_%'). This prevents tests from catching issues related to multiple '%' replacements in script commands. As the production code previously replaced all '%' instances, testing only single '%' usage reduces coverage of expected functionality.
rawFindings.suggestion: Add tests with multiple '%' placeholders in scripts to cover the use case of global replacements, ensuring future changes do not break multi-placeholder replacement.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect placeholder replacement with global flag in hook function
rawFindings.explanation: The original code uses a global regex /%/g to replace all occurrences of '%' in the script string with the joined package names string. The modification changes this to a non-global replacement, replacing only the first '%' occurrence. This changes the expected behavior where scripts can have multiple '%' placeholders to replace multiple times. It effectively breaks scripts that rely on multiple placeholders to receive the full list of package names each time.
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to using a global regex /%/g to replace all '%' placeholders or document that only one placeholder is supported. If multiple replacements are expected, the global flag must be used.
